each candidate using the original retrieval score plus transparent lexical,
route, segment, and low-rating relevance signals. It keeps CI and demos fully

classes.name: HybridRetriever
classes.summary: Combine dense and lexical retrieval with weighted, normalized scores.
classes.description:
Each underlying retriever is queried for an enlarged candidate pool. Scores
are min-max normalized per result list so the two scales are comparable,
then combined as a weighted sum. Documents appearing in both lists are
de-duplicated by chunk ID and receive contributions from both retrievers.

returns normalised vectors, so search can use a simple dot product.

methods.summary: Remove all chunks whose source document ID is in ``source_ids``.
methods.description:
Returns the number of chunks removed. This supports incremental updates:
a refreshed feedback record can replace every old chunk for the same
``feedback_id`` before the new chunks are appended.

methods.summary: Replace existing source documents and append the new chunks.
methods.description:
The replacement key is ``DocumentChunk.source_id``. All old chunks for
any incoming source are removed first, which handles changed text that
produces a different number of chunks.

optional Qdrant-backed store satisfy this protocol, so the retrieval layer
can treat them interchangeably. Vectors are assumed to be L2-normalised and
scored by cosine similarity, with higher scores meaning more similar.
